solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Base is where you'd expect it to be

definitions.meaning: a base act is mean, despicable, dirty

definitions.text: where you'd expect it to be
definitions.meaning: a base, the bottom of a thing, sits at the lowest level, right underneath

explanation.surface: A remark about something sitting in its proper place, as if foundations are reassuringly predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated phrase works as an adjective (contemptible) and, read literally, as the position at the bottom where a base belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Base meaning contemptible matches the informal adjective for underhand behaviour; the literal phrase describes the bottom position.

clue.text: Alison and I contrived to have an affair

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people, Alison and the speaker, engineer a romantic fling.
explanation.definitionFit: A clandestine romantic relationship is commonly called an illicit liaison, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Plane forever!

definitions.meaning: a plane is a planet without its last letter: a world with its end removed
the liturgical phrase from the doxology means for all eternity

explanation.surface: An exclamation of devotion to aircraft, as if wishing flying would never stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: PLANET loses its final T, so a plane is literally a world (planet) without its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase closing the Gloria Patri prayer means eternally, without ever ceasing.

clue.text: Former pupil occasionally loses instrument

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: occasionally means only some of the letters of loses are used, every other one

explanation.surface: An old student now and then mislays a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The double-reed woodwind of the orchestra is an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Girl's in mounting shock seeing strippers

indicators.note: in says the girl's name sits inside the reversed word
in a down clue mounting means rising, so the word for shock is read bottom to top

parts.note: to shock someone is to stun them
Di is a girl's name, with the S from the apostrophe S

explanation.surface: A girl is caught up in a growing scandal on witnessing a strip show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounting' reads upwards, so the word for shock turns into NUTS; 'in' puts the girl's name with its S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: People who take off all their clothes, naturists, are strippers in the loose sense of those who strip.

clue.text: Character showing concern about small library

indicators.note: about says the word for concern goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: care is worry or concern
LIB is an abbreviation of library

explanation.surface: Someone reveals their worth by fretting over a modest local library.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre means quality of mind or worth, the same sense as a person's character or standing.

clue.text: Act out sequence in garment

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of act are disordered

parts.note: in cards a suit is a sequence or set of the same kind

explanation.surface: An instruction to perform a series of moves while wearing a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece skintight outfit is a type of garment.

clue.text: Ladies maybe initially perform this aerobatic manoeuvre

parts.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, an example of a loo

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of perform

explanation.surface: Women perhaps first try out a stunt in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is British slang for a toilet; the Ladies is the women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying a complete vertical circle is a classic aerobatic stunt of this name.

clue.text: BC expanded into Canadian territory

parts.note: BC is the standard abbreviation of the westernmost Canadian province; written out in full it names it

explanation.surface: As if the era before Christ grew into a stretch of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: BC wants to be 'before Christ'; here it is the postal abbreviation of a Canadian province, expanded into its full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific province of Canada, with Victoria as capital, is abbreviated BC.

clue.text: Make deep impression in English party

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Someone makes a lasting mark at an English celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve lettering into a surface is to cut a deep impression into it.

clue.text: This might lower temperature if, for example, used in open debate

indicators.note: used in says the condition sits inside the word for open debate

parts.note: an airing is a public discussion of an issue
if introduces a condition, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: A conditional word in a public argument might cool things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' looks like part of the surface's logic but is the thing defined by example: a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling systems in buildings bring the temperature down.

clue.text: Note promotion about soft drink

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: about turns the word for promotion around

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: A memo concerning the marketing of a fizzy beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy mixer such as club water is a non-alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Children in dispute

definitions.meaning: a point of contention or matter being argued

explanation.surface: Kids involved in an argument, as in a custody fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring and a contested point are both legitimate senses of this one noun.

clue.text: Pray I have in part returned greeting

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A worshipper hoping a salutation has come back to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal hello is a casual greeting.

clue.text: Fruit juice for tennis star

definitions.meaning: a fermented drink made from pears
Fred ... won Wimbledon three times in the 1930s

explanation.surface: A sports drink associated with a famous player.
explanation.definitionFit: Pear cider is fermented fruit juice; the surname is that of the English tennis champion.

clue.text: Search question is written in French

parts.note: QU is a standard abbreviation of question; that these letters also open the word question itself is a coincidence
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A query about looking for something, phrased in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pursuit after something sought is a search.

clue.text: Fixers showing new adaptation of serial

indicators.note: an adaptation changes something, so the letters of serial are rearranged

explanation.surface: People who sort problems out reveal a fresh version of a TV serial.
explanation.definitionFit: People who fasten things with nails are literally fixers.

clue.text: This is one item of clothing to cover over yuck

indicators.note: to cover says the item of clothing is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a tie is an item worn round the neck
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ugh is an exclamation of disgust, like yuck

explanation.surface: A self-referential puzzle about putting a garment over something disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the puzzle itself, a Telegraph Toughie; 'is one' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle in hand is a Telegraph Toughie, a hard crossword, so the clue points at itself.

clue.text: Lively movement of coloured horse prancing around zone

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters surround the zone letter
prancing suggests jumping about, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: C is an abbreviation of coloured
taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A piebald horse cavorting about a field makes a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prancing' shuffles C and HORSE into SCHERO, which goes around Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful, quick section of a symphony or sonata is a lively movement.

clue.text: Don't move as guy starts to push us together

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to brace, a stay

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An order to stay still while a man begins to shove everyone together.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy rope and a stay both brace a mast or tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining where you are is the idiom for not moving.

clue.text: Burden of work on newspapers

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the press collectively means newspapers

explanation.surface: The weight of a job dealing with the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh down people with hardship is to burden them.

clue.text: Disagreement after party leads to riotous din

indicators.note: after places the leading letters behind the party word

parts.note: a disco is a dancing party

indicators.note: leads to takes the first letters of riotous and din

explanation.surface: An argument erupting after a party that grew too noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or lack of harmony between people is disagreement.

clue.text: Discharge soldiers — dull-looking one's uncomplaining

definitions.note: means one who is uncomplaining, a person who submits to being trodden on

parts.note: to discharge a duty is to do it
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
mat (matt) means without shine

explanation.surface: A command to dismiss troops, with a remark about a drab, docile person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone others walk all over without protest is figuratively a mat by the door.

clue.text: Stranger visiting outskirts of Derby becomes unsteady

indicators.note: visiting says the comparative goes inside those edge letters
outskirts are the edges, so just the first and last letters of Derby

parts.note: odder means more strange

explanation.surface: An oddball visitor to the edge of an English city starts to totter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaky and tottery from age, as of an old person, means unsteady.

clue.text: Answer objection to border

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Responding to a complaint about a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie adjacent to a neighbouring property is to border it.

clue.text: Bobbin's small 6 rising

indicators.note: rising in an across clue means reading the word backwards

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, an aerobatic manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A thread reel referring to a cross-reference climbing upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A cylinder on which thread is wound is a bobbin or reel.

clue.text: One of four in court

definitions.meaning: short for quadruplet, one of four born at a birth
short for quadrangle, a college courtyard

explanation.surface: A defendant among four in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form serves both for a quadruplet and for a quadrangle or courtyard.

clue.text: Note there's a thousand heading march, not five hundred

indicators.note: heading places the numeral at the top of the down entry

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: not says the numeral is removed

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A message about a thousand protesters leading a march, with five hundred missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes D from DEMO, leaving EMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written message is a note.

clue.text: Outspoken relative betting one might up this

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word for relative is pronounced

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: A blunt aunt who gambles and might raise the stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, players raise the stake put into the pot before a deal.

clue.text: Pressure on corrupt men with earlier debt that can be settled beforehand

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Pushing dishonest men who already owe money into a fixed deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being decided or fixed in advance.

clue.text: Old interrupting suited characters turned out to be boring

indicators.note: interrupting says the letter for old breaks into the shuffled letters
the characters, or letters, of suited are turned out of their order

explanation.surface: An old man breaks into a group of well-dressed figures who prove dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters turned out' shuffles SUITED to TEDIUS, which O interrupts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome and monotonous, lacking interest.

clue.text: Treatment of people in general holding chat

indicators.note: holding says the general pronoun contains the chat word

parts.note: they is used for people in general, as in they say
to rap is to talk or chat

explanation.surface: A session where ordinary people talk through their problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing work such as counselling is a form of treatment.
